Our channel's explainers: editorial paper cut-outs over the speaker, busy and animated.
prompt: This is a section of a lecture by neuroscientist Lisa Genzel of Radboud University on how memory works. Turn it into an explainer for our channel: tighten out the pauses, put a title on it, introduce her with a name card when she's first on camera, call out the key points as she makes them, explain her main concepts visually instead of leaving it all to her talking, and caption the whole thing. The project is already set up in our channel's style.

checklist.description: A title-role overlay opens the video and holds at least 3 s
A lower third names her while she is first on camera (before 25 s) and holds at least 4 s
Two or more callouts, each up at least 3 s
The title, the name card and the callouts are Motif layers (an example, a fork or the agent's own)
Pauses came out: less footage than the 215 s source, but not gutted
No A-roll clip shorter than 1 s
Picture runs without black holes
Each kept segment keeps its own sound
A caption track with a real number of cues
Captions run through the clip
Every caption sits over footage
At least three animated scenes (the pace asks one per minute of a ~3 min cut): Groups over the A roll, each at least 4 s
Every scene shows its idea in a picture (a sticker of a pool image or a still from the footage, or a drawing), and words label it
Most jump cuts left by tightening are covered by a scene, an insert or a punch-in (provisional: H2 left 97-100% bare)
No stretch over 12 s with nothing on screen but the speaker (the pace's bare_talk_max_s)
Something new arrives on screen at least every 8 s (the pace's beat_every_s)
At least a third of the graphic elements are pictures (titles, name cards and plates aside)
No scene or plate hides the captions
Scenes and plates cover at most half the cut
Overlays add what the speech does not, never the line being said
The overlays read as one clipping look: palette, fonts, spring, paper
Overlays and the insert leave by being taken off or sliding out, not by hard cuts
Overlays leave her face clear
A quote overlay uses her exact words
